text:
Amy (CS): Morning team — HarvestAI weekly health check. Quick summary: streaming reduces p95 on chat-route but we see p99 tail regressions on long-session traffic. Sync endpoints have slightly higher p95 but more stable p99. Spend is up ~12% last 7d due to longer streaming sessions.

Ben TSE: thanks — can you paste the raw numbers?

Amy (CS): sure, pulled last 7d window (UTC). Paste below.

```
chat-route (model: harvest-chat-v2)
  streaming: p95=240ms  p99=1.12s  errors=0.18%  reqs=68k/day
  sync:      p95=360ms  p99=900ms   errors=0.09%  reqs=22k/day

qa-route (model: harvest-qa-small)
  streaming: p95=310ms  p99=1.9s   errors=0.5%   reqs=8k/day
  sync:      p95=420ms  p99=2.0s   errors=0.6%   reqs=4k/day

embed-route (model: embed-lite-1)
  streaming: p95=85ms   p99=220ms  errors=0.04%  reqs=120k/day
  sync:      p95=78ms   p99=210ms  errors=0.03%  reqs=30k/day
```

Amy (CS): notes: chat-route streaming p95 advantage likely from KV cache reuse and early token dispatch. p99 increase seems correlated with sessions that keep context > 1600 tokens (cache churn).

Devon (SRE): I see corresponding SLO breaches in the last 48h around 03:00-05:00 UTC for the chat-route p99 spikes. Investigating hosts that had long GC pauses + occasional OOM logs.

Lina (Product): From the customer side, HarvestAI started a pilot of persistent user chat sessions last week — that aligns with the longer contexts. They mentioned using streaming to keep UI snappy.

Ben TSE: Cost note: streaming token billable tokens increased by +12% week-over-week, mainly from chat-route sessions that stream 3x more tokens per session.

Amy (CS): high-level risk: renewal risk small but rising if p99 keeps spiking for interactive users. They flagged a support ticket complaining about long response blips (case #5421).

Devon (SRE): action item: I'll add a tail-sampling trace and enable higher-res p99 histograms for chat-route, starting now. Also rolling a GC patch to two suspect hosts. ETA 2h.

Ben TSE: action item for infra: can we add a fallback policy to route requests with >1600 token context to the larger-memory pool to avoid cache thrash?

Devon (SRE): yes we can add a routing rule (policy: context_len>1600 -> big-pool). Will stage canary tonight.

Lina (Product): I'll ask HarvestAI PM to trial a client-side soft cap suggestion (nudge after 1200 tokens). Keeps UX but reduces tail.

Amy (CS): onboarding note: OnboardBot reminder — HarvestAI enablement session tomorrow 11am PT. @Devon please join for ops Q&A.

OnboardBot: Reminder set: "HarvestAI enablement" — Tomorrow 11:00 PT. :bell:

Amy (CS): next check-in: same time next week or sooner if SRE finds root cause. Thanks all :thumbsup:

Ben TSE: ack :+1:
